title: us_short_account_state
description: Manual US-short account/position state, produced by the manual-tables converter and (later) consumed by the US-short weekly report for holdings re-evaluation. User-maintained local input only: it does NOT connect to brokers, place orders, fetch account/market data, or authorize real-money automation. US-short bucket capital = us_market_equity / 3 (the system computes it; it never guesses from a vague total). v1 is long-only: every position carries direction=long (the marked door for a future independent short channel). This schema is US-short's own contract; it does NOT share the A-share a_short_account_state schema and uses US tickers (not A-share codes), with no A-share Rule12/Rule13 circuit-breaker/cooldown fields (US portfolio_guard / symbol_cooldown are paper-track / fill driven and derived later, not manual input).

us_market_equity.description: US market equity. The US-short bucket = this / 3 (per project capital policy).

us_short_bucket_capital.description: Computed = us_market_equity / 3. The sizing ceiling for the US-short bucket; the cross-field invariant (== us_market_equity/3) is enforced by validate_account_state, not by JSON Schema.

us_short_available_cash.description: Cash available to the US-short bucket (>= 0; a fully-deployed bucket can be 0). Must not exceed us_short_bucket_capital — bucket-local cash cannot be larger than the bucket (cross-field invariant enforced by validate_account_state; capital policy: per-market 1/3 buckets, A/US cash non-fungible).

portfolio_total_equity.description: Optional, reference only. Not used for sizing (per-market buckets are non-fungible).

ticker.description: US listing symbol (uppercase; optional .CLASS / -CLASS suffix, e.g. BRK.B). Must start with a letter, so A-share digit codes (e.g. 000001.SZ) are rejected.

direction.description: v1 long-only marked door (a future short channel needs its own borrow/locate/SSR/Reg SHO design).

current_stop.description: Optional user-recorded manual stop. The system computes its own stop levels later; this is the user's own reference, never a broker order.
